newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Soporcel considers new paper machine.
newsitem.headline: Soporcel considers new paper machine.

text.p: Portuguese pulp group Soporcel awaits word on possible financing by the European Investment Bank (EIB) before deciding whether to build a paper machine costing 63 billion escudos, its president said.

"The board will be able to take a final position about a second machine only after we know the financing conditions, namely from the EIB, and after agreeing investment conditions with the government," Soporcel president Alvaro Barreto said.
"We have everything planned to start in June 1998, but this depends on a final decision being taken by the end of November this year," he told Reuters in an interview.
State-owned bank Caixa Geral de Depositos owns 50.4 percent of Soporcel, Portugal's second biggest pulp producer. French group Arjo Wiggins owns 43.3 percent.

"There are contacts over the financing conditions, but they are still not concluded and should only be completed during November. Then we will take a final decision about a second machine," Barreto said.
A second paper machine would permit Soporcel's existing factory at Figueira da Foz in central Portugal to use its capacity fully.
Soporcel produces 400,000 tonnes of pulp a year, of which 180,000 are processed through its machine. The remainder is sold directly to the international pulp market.

Apart from the request for EIB financing, Soporcel has requested tax incentives totalling up to 12 billion escudos and other financial incentives for the investment, including professional training, Barreto said.
"We are hopeful that the EIB will support this project," Barreto said. "We asked the government for this investment contract just as we did for the first machine, but there is no decision so far."
He added: "We hope to reach an agreement with the government in November, but there is no commitment."
Barreto said Soporcel had discussed the possibility that the EIB would provide 50 percent of the financing for the project.
Soporcel shares stood at 3,760 escudos, up 10, at 1135 GMT.
